bank.prompt: The pawn on c5 is standing in front of your rook on c1. Win a piece.
bank.reason: cxd6 takes the knight and opens the c-file on to the queen on c8. exd6 answers, but then Rxc8 wins her.

bank.prompt: The pawn on e5 hides your rook on e1 from the black queen on e8. Win a piece.
bank.reason: exd6 takes the bishop and opens the file. cxd6 would hand over the queen to Rxe8.

bank.prompt: Your rook on d1 is behind your own pawn on d5. Take the knight.
bank.reason: dxe6 wins the knight and opens the d-file. The knight was the queen's only guard, so fxe6 runs into Rxd8.

bank.prompt: Your knight on d5 is standing in your own rook's way. Move it, and take something as you go.
bank.reason: Nxf4 wins the knight on f4 and turns the rook on d1 on to the queen on d8 at the same moment.

bank.prompt: Tap the white piece that attacks the black queen the moment the knight on d5 moves away.
bank.reason: The rook on d1. It is already on the queen's file, with only your own knight in the way.

bank.prompt: White plays exd6 and Black recaptures cxd6. What has Black overlooked?
options: The queen on e8 was already guarded twice.
The pawn on c7 was pinned and was not allowed to capture.
The rook on e1 now takes the queen on e8 for nothing.
bank.reason: The knight on d6 was the queen's only guard. Once the pawn takes its place the queen is alone on an open file.

bank.prompt: White jumps the knight to b6, opening the d-file behind it. Is the knight safe on b6?
reasons: No. The pawn on b7 takes it.
No. The rook on a8 takes it.
bank.reason: The knight's move was free, so it had to buy something: it hits the rook on a8 and the bishop on c8, and behind it the rook on d1 hits the undefended rook on d8.

bank.prompt: Tap the two white pieces that are standing on the d-file.
bank.reason: The rook on d1 and the knight on d5. The knight is the door; the rook is the attack behind it.

bank.prompt: Tap the black piece that comes under attack the moment the pawn on e5 captures.
bank.reason: The queen on e8. She is on the same file as the rook on e1, and only the white pawn is in between.

bank.prompt: Tap the white rook that is waiting behind the pawn on c5.
bank.reason: The rook on c1. The pawn is the only thing between it and the black queen on c8.

bank.prompt: Tap the square your pawn on d5 should capture on.
bank.reason: e6. The pawn takes a knight and steps off the d-file, so the rook on d1 hits the queen.

bank.prompt: Every move the knight on d5 makes opens the d-file. What decides which one to play?
options: Any of them is equally good, because the file opens either way.
Play the one that takes the knight furthest from your own king.
Play the one that wins something as it goes.
bank.reason: The file opens whatever the knight does, so the knight's own move is free. Spend it on a capture.

bank.prompt: The black queen on c6 is guarded three times. Take her anyway.
bank.reason: Nxc6 uncovers the rook's check on e8. Every one of the three guards would have to ignore the check, so none of them may take.

bank.prompt: Win the black knight on g6.
bank.reason: Nxg6 opens the rook's check on the king, so neither the f7 nor the h7 pawn may take back.

bank.prompt: Your queen on e1 is aimed down the file at the black king. Move the knight and win the black queen.
bank.reason: It does not have to be a rook behind. Nxg6 uncovers the white queen's check, and the pawns on f7 and h7 may not recapture.

bank.prompt: Tap the white piece that is hiding the rook on e1 from the black king.
bank.reason: The knight on e5. While it stands there the king is safe; the moment it moves, the rook is giving check.

bank.prompt: After Nxc6, why can Black not reply bxc6?
options: The pawn on b7 is pinned by the bishop on d3.
The king on e8 is in check, and bxc6 does not answer the check.
bxc6 is not a legal pawn capture.
bank.reason: A move made while your king is in check has to deal with the check. Taking on c6 leaves the rook still attacking e8.

bank.prompt: White takes the pawn on f7 with the same idea. Is the knight safe there?
reasons: No. The king on e8 takes it and answers the check in the same move.
Yes. Black is in check, so nothing may capture it.
No. The pawn on g7 takes it.
bank.reason: Kxf7 steps off the e-file and captures at once, so it is a legal answer to the check. g6 was the square, not f7.

bank.prompt: Tap the black piece that is lost as soon as the knight on e5 moves with check.
bank.reason: The queen on d7. The knight can reach her, and of the three guards only the king may take back — queen for knight.

bank.prompt: The queen on d7 is guarded by a bishop, a knight and the king. Why is she still lost after Nxd7?
options: The bishop on c8 is pinned to the king.
Only the king can capture and answer the check at once, and that is a queen for a knight.
The knight on b8 has no legal moves.
bank.reason: Guards are only guards if they are allowed to move. Two of these three are not, while the king is in check.

bank.prompt: The bishop on e5 hides the rook on e1 from the king on e8. What does Bxc7 do?
options: It takes the queen and uncovers the rook's check in one move.
It gives check with the bishop itself.
It defends the rook on e1.
bank.reason: The bishop on c7 is not attacking the king at all. The check comes from the rook it has just stopped blocking.

bank.prompt: Tap the white piece that gives check the moment the knight leaves e5.
bank.reason: The queen on e1. The piece hiding behind the front man does not have to be a rook.

bank.prompt: The knight steps to g6, opening the rook's check on the e-file. Is the knight safe on g6?
reasons: No. The pawn on f7 takes it.
No. The rook on h8 takes it.
Yes. Black is in check from the rook on e1, so the pawn on f7 is not allowed to move.
bank.reason: The f7 pawn does guard g6, and it is not allowed to use the guard: every legal answer to a check must stop the check. Whatever Black plays, Nxh8 follows.

bank.prompt: White plays Nxg6. Which of these is true?
options: Black is in check from the rook, so neither pawn may take the knight.
Black may reply hxg6 and come out a piece ahead.
The knight on g6 is the piece giving the check.
bank.reason: The check comes from the rook on e1 down the open file. The knight is only the piece that stopped blocking it.

bank.prompt: The rook on d2 and the queen on d1 are lined up on the same file. Win material.
bank.reason: Rxd7 Nxd7 Qxd7. You give a rook and take a rook and a knight, which is a piece ahead.

bank.prompt: The black rook on d5 has one guard and you have two attackers on the file. Win material.
bank.reason: Rxd5 Nxd5 Qxd5. Two attackers against one defender wins the extra piece.

bank.prompt: Tap the two white pieces that are lined up one behind the other on the d-file.
bank.reason: The queen on d1 and the rook on d2. The rook goes in first and the queen takes over.

bank.prompt: Tap the only square on the d-file that the rook on f2 can reach.
bank.reason: d2. It slides along the second rank and lands directly in front of the rook on d1.

bank.prompt: The rook on d5 is guarded once, by the knight on f6. Why does Rxd5 win material?
options: Two attackers against one defender: the second rook takes again.
The knight on f6 is pinned and cannot recapture.
The rook on d5 has no square to run to.
bank.reason: Count attackers and defenders before you capture. Two against one wins whatever is standing there.

bank.prompt: Tap the black piece that is guarding the rook on d5.
bank.reason: The knight on f6. It is the only defender, which is why two attackers are enough.

bank.prompt: White captures on d5. Is the rook safe there?
reasons: No. The knight on f6 takes it, and the queen on d1 takes back.
Yes. Nothing attacks d5 any more.
No. The rook on f8 takes it.
bank.reason: It is not safe, and it does not need to be. The piece behind it recaptures and you come out a knight ahead.

bank.prompt: Tap the white piece standing behind the queen on d2.
bank.reason: The rook on d1. Because it is there, the queen may walk into d8 where the rook on f8 can take her.

bank.prompt: What does moving the rook from f2 to d2 achieve?
options: It puts the black king on g8 in check.
It adds a second attacker to the black rook on d7.
It stops the knight on b8 from moving.
bank.reason: One attacker against one defender is nothing. Two against one wins the rook on d7.

bank.prompt: Tap the white rook that does the capturing on d7 first.
bank.reason: The rook on d2, the one in front. The rook on d1 waits behind it and takes back afterwards.

bank.prompt: Tap the two white pieces that share the d-file.
bank.reason: The rooks on d1 and d2. Between them they attack d5 twice, and only the knight on f6 defends it.
